### Stratégie, politiques et pratiques

#### Stratégie de développement durable

La Technological University Dublin (TU Dublin) a déclaré avoir mis en place une stratégie de développement durable. Cette stratégie est définie dans le TU Dublin Strategic Plan, qui comprend des objectifs de durabilité mesurables. Le vice-président de la durabilité est le sponsor de ces objectifs, tandis que Rosie Webb en est la responsable.

(GRI 2-22)

#### Engagements politiques

La TU Dublin a déclaré avoir mis en place des engagements politiques pour promouvoir la durabilité. Ces engagements sont définis dans le TU Dublin Strategic Plan et sont axés sur la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre et l'augmentation de l'efficacité énergétique. Les activités de durabilité menées par les SECs (Student Employers' Councils) sont également un exemple d'engagement politique. (GRI 2-23)

#### Processus de remédiation des impacts négatifs

La TU Dublin a déclaré avoir mis en place un processus de remédiation des impacts négatifs. Ce processus est axé sur la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre et l'augmentation de l'efficacité énergétique. Les activités de durabilité menées par les SECs sont également un exemple de processus de remédiation. (GRI 2-25)

#### Adhésion à des associations

La TU Dublin a déclaré avoir adhéré à des associations pour promouvoir la durabilité. Cependant, il est important de noter que la TU Dublin n'a pas adhéré à des associations de manière générale, mais plutôt a signé des chartes et des engagements spécifiques. (GRI 2-28)

#### Limites et omissions

evidence.text: [n]. TU Dublin Strategic Plan [n] – [n] (Ref [n]) include clear measurable sustainability objectives for which the sponsor is the VP of Sustainability, and the lead is Rosie Webb. In page [n], our campus related targets are [n]% reduction in GHG emissions by [n], and [n]% increase in energy efficiency by [n]. These targets are in line with the Climate Action Plan [n] (CAP[n]) whereby the public sector must lead by example on climate action to reach the target of reducing Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions by [n]% by [n] and becoming climate neutral no later than [n]. (Ref [n])

through and with the SECs TU Dublin members conduct climate resilience activities. SEC activities include the decarbonisation of the building environment (e.g. façade upgrades, integration of renewable sources and heat pumps), the development of sustainable transportation project (e.g. raising issues on public transport, calling for the development of bike lanes, free bike repairs to the communities, supporting the installation of bike shelters), the greening of space and biodiversity actions (e.g. avoiding trees being destroyed for the development of a new drive lane, adding trees and green spaces in communities). See for example this article about the Cabra SEC and their flood alleviation

The Sustainability Education team offer Continuing Professional Devlopment (CDP) on sustainability (Ref[n]). The team also runs the Sustainability Education Symposium with an emphasis on how the competences set out in the EU GreenComp framework can be integrated into Teaching-Learning-Assessment (TLA) design, the symposium is an opportunity for educators from across the University to hear from colleagues who will share teaching, learning and assessment practices which support the development of sustainability-focused global citizens (Ref[n]).

The Green Campus Committee and Programme encourages a partnership approach to environmental education, management, and action in [n]-level institutions. The programme primarily aims to ensure that members of a campus community can engage in a meaningful way to enhance sustainability on campus (Ref[n]). The SDG Literacy Community of Practice aims to empower faculty and students to co-create learning opportunities that will build knowledge of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and enable students to make meaningful connections between the SDGs and their focus of study (Ref[n]).
